page_placements.theme: Validity of absorption and splitting metrics and detectors

record.tranche_reason: The post applies an ablation-based search for feature absorption and reports that its proposed signal does not reliably identify absorption-like pairs. It refines the evidence for absorption, but does not test dictionary-size scaling or the full parent-child splitting claim.
record.gate_note: The post reports its own experiment on Gemma-2-2b: it ablates SAE latents, measures their effects on a later SAE, and checks for non-co-occurring candidate pairs. Theoretical examples and cited results are not recorded as rows. The sanity check of strong causal links is mentioned but does not report a separate result bearing on the claim.
record.test_reason: The post proposes a way to detect absorption: non-co-occurring SAE latents with similar downstream ablation effects. It reports only that this detector performs poorly. It never measures how often or how strongly absorption, splitting, or parent latents failing to fire occur in Gemma-2-2b SAEs. This is a detection-method study with no rate of the behaviour, so it does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors find that effect-vector cosine similarity does not currently identify absorption well. They suggest other metrics, such as Jaccard, gradient attribution, and toy models to tell absorption apart from splitting.
record.recipe_differences: The post proposes an automatic detection method based on ablation effects and co-occurrence, rather than testing the original feature-splitting method or measuring splits across dictionary sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: The post notes that candidate pairs may actually co-occur despite the dataset's ~1e6 prompts; it suggests that more data may help with coincidental causal similarities but may not fix missed co-occurrence.

fits_no_version.finding: On Gemma-2-2b with Gemma Scope SAEs (L20 MLP to L21 residual), cosine similarity of ablation effect vectors between non-co-occurring latents is not bimodal. It does not strongly track subjectively judged absorption, and candidates include unrelated pairs, pairs that actually co-occur, and single-token latent pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream causal-effect similarity between mutually exclusive SAE latents is not a reliable automatic detector of feature absorption.

record.problems: The post describes failure modes qualitatively without counts or uncertainty estimates. It states that the proposed metric does not correlate strongly with subjective judgments of absorption, and the co-occurrence data may still miss pairs that co-occur in constructed prompts.
record.rows_left_out: No separate row for the causal-link sanity check: the post says the strongest links mostly connect latents with plausibly related meanings, but provides no separate numerical result.

untested.parts: No comparison of dictionary sizes or coarse-to-fine replacement.
No measurement of splitting in large models or across SAE families; Gemma Scope SAEs are used only as the tool.
No test of nested or geometrically close feature families mirroring a hierarchy.
No measurement of parent latents failing to fire where child latents take over, and no variation of SAE size or sparsity. Only a theoretical toy model is given, plus a detector that fails.
No comparison of larger and smaller SAE latents for decomposition or novel latents.
No comparison of training objectives. The toy model argues that L0 minimisation produces absorption but is not tested empirically.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T5 and its V4 limits_scope label should be dropped. The failure of a detector is not evidence that absorption is absent or limited; the post itself assumes absorption exists. The theoretical subset and intersection lemmas are toy constructions, not results on models.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not compare SAE dictionary sizes or test whether smaller features are replaced by several finer features.
It tests one model and does not test large models or open SAE releases as evidence for size-related splitting.
It does not test nested feature families or whether they mirror a concept hierarchy.

The experiment searches for non-co-occurring latents with similar downstream effects, but does not establish parent-child feature identities, test a hierarchical split directly, or vary SAE size or sparsity.
It does not compare larger and smaller dictionaries for combinations of latents or novel latents.
It does not compare training objectives or test whether an alternative objective changes splitting.

rows.subject: google/gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Ablate Layer 20 MLP SAE latents; measure their downstream effects on Layer 21 residual SAE latents and compare effect-vector cosine similarity with subjective assessments of absorption.
rows.measure: Whether cosine similarity of downstream effect vectors predicts whether non-co-occurring latent pairs subjectively look like feature absorption.
rows.value: The histogram of effect-vector cosine similarities was not bimodal; examples that subjectively looked like feature absorption could be selected from both ends of the distribution; the metric was not strongly correlated with subjective absorption.
rows.note: This is evidence that the proposed marker is unreliable, not a direct measurement of whether a parent latent fails to fire when a child takes over.
rows.check: Measures how well the post's own detection metric (effect-vector cosine similarity) tracks subjective absorption. That is method performance, not whether absorption occurs. A non-bimodal histogram says nothing about V4's effect.

rows.subject: google/gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Inspect candidate non-co-occurring latent pairs returned by the ablation-based search.
rows.measure: Whether candidate latent pairs appear semantically related as feature absorption.
rows.value: One reported failure mode was that the script outputs two latents that do not seem related.
rows.note: The post gives this as a failure mode, without counts or named pairs.
rows.check: A qualitative failure mode of the detection script (unrelated pairs returned). It is method performance with no counts, not a measurement of absorption.

rows.subject: google/gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Check co-occurrence for candidate latent pairs returned by the ablation-based search.
rows.measure: Whether candidate pairs that were expected not to co-occur actually co-occur when tested with a constructed prompt.
rows.value: One reported failure mode was that candidate latents actually co-occur when a prompt is made up to test them; the post says the co-occurrence data already uses ~1e6 prompts.
rows.note: This failure mode is described qualitatively, without counts or a named pair.
rows.check: A qualitative failure mode of the detection script (candidate pairs actually co-occur). It is method performance, not evidence on whether parent latents fail to fire.

relation.reason: The post takes absorption as given and builds a detector for it. The detector's failure is method performance, not a test of V4.

tranche.reason: The post builds an absorption detector, reports only that it performs poorly, and never measures how often or how strongly absorption occurs. Its toy model restates the known mechanism; it is not a new result on a version.

source_check.notes: The post is negative only on its own detector (non-bimodal histogram, co-occurring or unrelated pairs, single-token pairs). It gives no counts and no quantitative absorption result. No rows cover the single-token failure mode or the sanity check (causal links mostly plausible). The reader's call (tests, T5) is wrong.

statements.problem: none; the text says the cosine-similarity histogram is not bimodal and the metric isn't strongly correlated with subjectively judged absorption, on Gemma-2-2b, Gemma Scope L20 MLP to L21 residual

reader_labels.condition: The tested Gemma-2-2b SAE pair and the proposed absorption-detection procedure
reader_labels.reason: The proposed causal-effect similarity signal did not reliably distinguish absorption-like pairs, and candidate pairs could be unrelated or co-occur; this limits what the experiment establishes about absorption. See r1-r3.
